title: P0 hostedapi session shear sleuthing notes
content:
Summary:

Short: On 2026-12-09 ~03:12 UTC Hosted API experienced a P0 degradation affecting streaming TTFB and an increase in 5xx for ~38 minutes. Impact: ~14% of active streaming sessions experienced repeated small fragments (stream-chop) and ~2.1% end-to-end request failures (5xx). Root cause: a combination of (1) a scheduler coalescing edge case that delayed session writeback under interleaved client multiplexing patterns and (2) accelerated KV-cache eviction due to a TTL miscalculation after a recent perf config change. Those two together created a feedback loop we labeled "session shear": sessions would intermittently pause, then flood with backlog when resuming causing per-node resource pressure and cascading connection resets.

What we saw (user-visible):
- Streaming clients reported many small chunks instead of steady chunked streaming; many clients retried and observed increased latency.
- P95/P99 TTFB increased by ~420ms/980ms on affected shard clusters.
- 5xx count for streaming endpoints rose to 2.1% of traffic vs baseline 0.02% during the incident window.
- Error patterns: upstream HTTP 503 / stream write errors + worker oom-kill traces in metrics.

Timeline (UTC):
- 03:08 - Gradual rise in TTFB alerts in eu-west-1 dashboard. Small noise but correlated with a new traffic pattern from a large customer.
- 03:12 - Pager fired (P0) when composite streaming SLO breach > 3 sequential minutes. Oncall -> Aisha paged.
- 03:14 - Confirmed 5xx spike and streaming fragmenting. Began mitigations: shift traffic from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 via routing policy to reduce blast radius.
- 03:18 - Observed edge proxies reporting frequent "write buffer full" and internal acceptor backlog growth.
- 03:22 - Linked worker pods started to show KV-cache eviction rate increase; process memory climbed then OOMs on the most-loaded nodes.
- 03:25 - Applied temporary throttling at edge (limit stream handshake rate for the largest tenant) and disabled a recently-enabled scheduler coalescing flag.
- 03:30 - Evictions steadied; OOMs ceased on rolling restarted nodes. TTFB began trending down.
- 03:50 - Full recovery; traffic routing normalized by 04:05.

Initial detection and signals used:
- Alerts: streaming-ttfb-p95-above-slo, streaming-5xx-rate, node-oom-rate.
- Dashboards: per-shard streaming throughput & latency, kv-cache eviction histogram, acceptor queue length, GC pause trends.
- Logs: proxy write buffer events, worker runtime OOM, scheduler coalescer debug traces.

Immediate mitigations taken (chronological):
1) Edge routing policy: shift ~33% traffic off the hottest shard cluster to neighboring regions to reduce local concurrency. (Miguel)
2) Apply handshake rate-limit to tenant X (largest traffic delta) to prevent mass reconnect storms. (Priya)
3) Roll restart of the three most-impacted worker node pools to break KV-cache hot shards and recover memory. (Oncall)
4) Toggle scheduler.coalesce=false in the runtime config to avoid delayed write batching under interleaved sessions. (Aisha)

Why those mitigations:
- Routing reduced immediate load per node and allowed memory and acceptor latencies to recover without wholesale global throttles.
- Handshake throttling prevented the flocking behavior where paused sessions resumed simultaneously.
- Disabling coalescing removed the latent batching behavior that worsened acceptor backlog when sessions were interleaved.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- Trigger: a tenant began a high degree of interleaved multiplexed streaming sessions (many concurrent half-open-ish streams with intermittent small writes).
- Primary failure mode: scheduler coalescer deferred writes to optimize throughput; combined with the tenant's pattern this increased per-connection buffering. When the runtime attempted to flush, bursts caused acceptor queue pressure and local memory spikes.
- Secondary amplification: a background config change in kv-cache TTL math (rolled out in a minor perf tweak to evict stale prefixes faster) introduced slightly shorter TTLs for prefix entries. That increased eviction churn under bursty access, removing helpful KV warmings and inflating CPU/memory due to rehydration.
- Feedback loop: flush bursts -> acceptor backlog -> retransmissions and reconnects -> KV rehydration -> memory pressure -> OOMs/connection resets -> more reconnects. We call this session shear.

Contributing factors (not root but material):
- The perf tweak to kv-cache TTL had insufficient canary exposure and metrics were not annotated in the rollout.
- No runbook step for the coalescing flag toggling under simultaneous handshake storm scenarios.
- The routing policy defaults favored locality which concentrated the tenant's atypical pattern onto a small set of shards.
- Edge client library in the tenant had an aggressive reconnect policy that retried too quickly on partial failures.

Evidence (samples):
- Example acceptor backlog snapshot (at 03:19): acceptor_queue_length{shard=s-13}=842, write_buf_full_events=1374m.
- KV eviction histogram delta: evictions/sec rose from 0.8 -> 14.6 during peak.
- Node memory: worker-node-7 resident_size jumped 1.1GB -> 6.3GB before OOM at 03:21.
- Logs: runtime[scheduler] INFO "coalesced_flush_delay=120ms" then "flush_fanout=large"; proxy WARN "write_buffer_full -> client-reset".

Post-incident changes (short-term / immediate):
- Reverted kv-cache TTL change in the last perf rollout (rollback id: rollout-2026-11-27-kvttl). (Owner: Platform-Infra)
- Add an automated canary check to detect >3x eviction/sec deltas during rollouts. (Owner: Platform-Infra)
- Update runbook: add a new play: "If streaming TTFB + eviction rate both spike, toggle scheduler.coalesce and consider partial routing". (Owner: SRE)
- Implement temporary default handshake backoff increase for tenants flagged as heavy multiplexers. (Owner: Customer Success + SRE)

Longer-term actions (with owners and tentative due dates):
- SRE-4521: Implement per-tenant streaming-rate shaping at the edge gateway (limit concurrent half-open sessions) — Owner: Miguel — Due: 2027-01-20.
- SRE-4522: Add eviction churn telemetry (per-prefix heatmap) and alerting for sustained increases — Owner: Priya — Due: 2026-12-22.
- RTE-317: Scheduler coalescer audit and improved heuristics (avoid coalescing for interleaved streams with low steady-state throughput) — Owner: Runtime Team (RTE) — Due: 2027-02-01.
- PLAT-790: Routing policy change: prefer diversity for new large tenants, avoid concentrating initial traffic on a single shard ring — Owner: Platform Eng — Due: 2027-01-10.
- DOCS-101: Runbook expansion and playbook page: "session shear" with clear triage steps, CLI commands and quick mitigations — Owner: Aisha — Due: 2026-12-15.

Runbook snippet to add (to keep handy during oncall):
- Symptom detection: streaming-ttfb-p95 > SLO AND streaming-5xx-rate increase > 0.5% AND kv-eviction-rate > baseline*3 for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Quick triage commands:
  - kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=worker -o wide --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
  - prometheus query: increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[2m]) / instance
  - check acceptor backlog: /api/diag/acceptor?shard=s-13
- Immediate actions (ordered):
  1) Shift 25-40% traffic off the affected shard via routing -> reduces per-node concurrency.
  2) If node memory > 80% and evictions spike: roll restart affected worker pool.
  3) Toggle scheduler.coalesce=false if acceptor backlog is growing despite routing.
  4) If reconnect storms continue: apply tenant handshake rate-limit and request app team to adopt backoff.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Was the tenant's client library recently updated? We need to ask Solutions Eng to get client version and reconnect behavior. (Ticket: SRE-4530)
- Can we simulate interleaved multiplexing patterns in staging to reproduce session shear? Need a test harness. (Engineering task created)
- Why did the TTL rollout not trigger our canary eviction metric? Investigate rollout config and missing metric annotation.

Notes to self (oncall heuristics):
- Look for the triad: TTFB spike + eviction spike + acceptor backlog; that combo equals high probability for session shear.
- Short-term toggles (coalesce flag) are safe fallback but we must coordinate with Runtime to avoid throughput regressions.
- In future, add a dashboard tile that overlays acceptor queue, eviction rate and per-tenant reconnect rate for quick eyeballing.

Communication & follow-up:
- Incident summary emailed to infra-all and to the tenant's SE with an apology and explanation of mitigations. (Draft saved to Confluence referenced above.)
- Postmortem review scheduled: 2026-12-14 16:00 UTC (invite: eng-sre, runtime, platform infra, solutions eng).
